name: Discord
short_description: Create a Discord application and use OAuth2 to identify users, read their servers, or add your bot.

guide_content.summary: Discord supports OAuth2 for applications created in the Discord Developer Portal. The authorization code grant lets users grant scopes such as identify, email and guilds; the bot scope adds your app's bot to a server. User-only OAuth needs no review. Separate review processes apply only to some cases: privileged gateway intents above a usage threshold, bot verification for large servers counts, and partner-only scopes.
guide_content.complexity_rationale: User OAuth (identify/guilds) is a single application plus redirect configuration with a standard code exchange. Complexity rises only if you add a bot that needs privileged intents at scale, or request partner-only scopes; those conditions are flagged below.

prerequisites.title: A Discord account
prerequisites.description: Needed to sign in to the Developer Portal and create an application. The fetched docs do not state further account requirements (such as email verification).

prerequisites.title: A test server (if you will add a bot)
prerequisites.description: Discord recommends testing server-installable apps in a server that isn't actively used by others; you can create one for free.

prerequisites.title: Note on team-owned applications
prerequisites.description: Team applications are limited to the identify and applications.commands.update scopes, because teams are not bound to a specific user.

setup_steps.title: Create an application
setup_steps.description: Signed in, open https://discord.com/developers/applications?new_application=true, enter a name and press Create. You land on General Information, which shows the Application ID.

setup_steps.title: Collect the client ID and client secret
setup_steps.description: Your application has a client_id and client_secret used by all OAuth2 endpoints. The fetched docs do not describe the exact portal screen for viewing or resetting the client secret; confirm it in the portal.

setup_steps.title: Register your redirect URI
setup_steps.description: redirect_uri must be a URL you registered for your application. The fetched docs do not name the portal page where redirects are registered.

setup_steps.title: Send users to the authorize URL
setup_steps.description: Redirect users to https://discord.com/oauth2/authorize with response_type=code, client_id, scope (e.g. identify guilds), state (highly recommended), redirect_uri and optionally prompt=consent.

setup_steps.title: Exchange the code for a token
setup_steps.description: POST to https://discord.com/api/oauth2/token as application/x-www-form-urlencoded (JSON is rejected) with grant_type=authorization_code, code and redirect_uri, authenticating with HTTP Basic or client_id/client_secret in the body. The example response shows a 604800-second (7-day) access token and a refresh token.

setup_steps.title: (Conditional) Configure bot installation
setup_steps.description: If you add a bot: on the Installation page select install contexts and, for Guild Install, add the applications.commands and bot scopes. The bot token is on the Bot page ("Reset Token"); it is shown only when regenerated.

setup_steps.title: (Conditional) Privileged intents
setup_steps.description: Bots needing GUILD_PRESENCES, GUILD_MEMBERS or MESSAGE_CONTENT toggle them on the Bot page. Under Discord's current review guide, apps above 10,000 users must apply for Privileged Intent access (within 90 days of notification) and reapply yearly.

permissions_scopes.name: email
permissions_scopes.condition_note: Only if you need the user's email.

permissions_scopes.name: guilds
permissions_scopes.explanation: Lets /users/@me/guilds return basic information about all of a user's servers.
permissions_scopes.condition_note: Only if you list the user's servers.

permissions_scopes.name: guilds.join
permissions_scopes.explanation: Lets your app add the user to a server. Your bot must already be in that server.
permissions_scopes.condition_note: Only for joining users to servers.

permissions_scopes.name: bot
permissions_scopes.explanation: Puts your app's bot in the server the user selects.
permissions_scopes.condition_note: Only if you have a bot.

permissions_scopes.name: applications.commands
permissions_scopes.explanation: Lets your app add commands to a server; included by default with bot.

permissions_scopes.name: connections
permissions_scopes.explanation: Lets /users/@me/connections return the user's linked third-party accounts.
permissions_scopes.condition_note: Only if you need linked accounts.

permissions_scopes.name: Partner-only scopes (e.g. rpc, voice, dm_channels.read)
permissions_scopes.explanation: Discord lists several scopes as only available to approved partners; requesting them without approval may cause errors.

credentials_configuration.name: Client ID (Application ID)
credentials_configuration.description: Used in authorize URLs and token requests.
credentials_configuration.where_obtained: Developer Portal → your application → General Information.

credentials_configuration.name: Client secret
credentials_configuration.description: Authenticates your app to the token and revoke endpoints.
credentials_configuration.where_obtained: Your application in the Developer Portal (exact screen not described in fetched docs). Backend only.

credentials_configuration.name: Redirect URI(s)
credentials_configuration.description: Must be registered for your application and sent URL-encoded in redirect_uri.
credentials_configuration.where_obtained: Developer Portal (page not named in fetched docs).

credentials_configuration.name: Bot token (only if you have a bot)
credentials_configuration.description: Authenticates your bot user; highly sensitive and different from the client secret and user access tokens.
credentials_configuration.where_obtained: Developer Portal → Bot page → Reset Token. Shown only once per reset.

time_approval.active_effort_basis: Creating the application, registering a redirect URI and recording credentials; more if you also configure a bot and install settings. Excludes integration code. Not published by Discord.
time_approval.review_requirement_explanation: No review for user OAuth with standard scopes. Conditional reviews: (1) Privileged Intent access for apps above 10,000 users (current review guide); (2) app verification for bots in 100+ servers, per the Gateway page (older wording that conflicts with the new threshold); (3) approval for partner-only scopes.

review_wait.summary: Unknown. Discord's review guide gives a 90-day window to apply after notification, but no review turnaround time was found. The verification help article could not be accessed.

time_approval.elapsed_time_note: User OAuth: elapsed time is about the active effort. Bots that cross review thresholds may wait on Discord review (duration Unknown).

agent_can_do: Find and compare Discord's OAuth2, getting-started, gateway and intent-review documentation.
Flag conflicting review thresholds between Discord pages.
Extract endpoints, scope descriptions and token rules.
Attempt to view the Developer Portal without signing in and record the result.
human_must_do: Sign in to Discord and create the application (accepting Discord's developer terms where prompted).
Register redirect URIs; obtain and store the client secret (and bot token, if any).
Configure installation settings and privileged intents for bots.
Apply for Privileged Intent access or verification if Discord notifies you.
Note: end users separately consent to your scopes; server admins choose whether to add your bot.

portal_exploration.human_handoff: Sign in to Discord, open https://discord.com/developers/applications?new_application=true, name the application and press Create; then register your redirect URI and note the client ID and secret.
portal_exploration.sandbox_or_test_mode: No sandbox mode was found. Discord recommends testing on your own account and in a server that isn't actively used by others.

composio_managed_oauth.explanation: Composio's Discord toolkit page lists OAUTH2 and states "Composio-managed OAuth available? Yes"; the managed-auth catalog lists both Discord and a separate Discord Bot toolkit.
when_to_bring_own_app: You want your own app name on Discord's consent screen.
You need custom scopes or a dedicated rate-limit quota.
You need polling faster than managed auth's 2-minute minimum interval.

common_issues.explanation: The token and revoke URLs only accept application/x-www-form-urlencoded.
The token lacks a scope required by the endpoint.
common_issues.resolution: Request the needed scope and have the user re-authorize.

common_issues.explanation: The client secret sent is invalid.
common_issues.resolution: Double-check what you send, or regenerate your client secret.
Generate and verify state per request.

common_issues.explanation: Your bot requested an intent that is not enabled or approved.
common_issues.resolution: Enable the intent on the Bot page (or apply for access if above the review threshold) and match it in code.

common_issues.explanation: Revoking any token revokes all active access and refresh tokens for that authorization.
common_issues.resolution: Only revoke when you intend to fully disconnect the user.

evidence_notes.claim: Privileged Intent review threshold is now user-based (above 10,000 users), as of June 10, 2026.
Bots in 100+ servers require verification (older Gateway-page wording, conflicts with the new user-based threshold).
Example access token lifetime of 604800 seconds (7 days).
PKCE support at the token endpoint.
Composio-managed OAuth is available for Discord.

tested_status.notes: No Discord application was created and no authorization flow was run. All Verified labels are documentation-based.

checklist_items.label: Create the application in the Developer Portal
Store the client secret (and bot token, if any) server-side
Choose minimal scopes; avoid partner-only scopes
Implement the authorize redirect with state
Implement form-encoded token exchange and refresh
(If bot) Configure Installation settings and intents
(If bot at scale) Watch for Privileged Intent review notifications
